strengths: Edge CV deployment is a direct hit: TensorRT-optimized YOLO on Jetson at 5.2x speedup (56.7->10.9 ms) is exactly the 'push inference onto roadside hardware, fast/small/power-efficient' half of the role.

Classical-vs-heavy-model judgment is genuinely evidenced at BARC: custom sym6+bior3.5 wavelet bank + bit-manipulation stitching reached PSNR 86 where a homography baseline gave 65 — he picked a filter over a network and it won.

Dataset collection and curation at source: CARLA semantic-segmentation + raycast occlusion pipeline produced ~5,000 YOLO and ~3,000 UFLD frames with zero manual annotation; Tusk dataset curated and annotated by hand to 83% mAP@50.

Physical-world robustness: resolved 11 integration failures (false positives, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture) to 100% pick reliability — this is the 'systems that stand up to the unpredictability of the physical world' ask.
Efficiency without accuracy loss: 8-bit LLM.int8 quantization cut GPU memory ~55% with <1% accuracy degradation; CUDA kernel work gave ~35% speedup over naive GPU.
real_gaps: No model has ever served production traffic — the JD's mission line is 'ships the model, not just trains it', and every deployment in the profile terminates at a capstone demo, a mobile export, or a benchmark.
No deployment monitoring, drift detection, retraining loop, or post-ship iteration anywhere in the profile.
No re-identification or metric learning (triplet/contrastive/embedding search); embeddings appear only as transformer internals.
Scale mismatch: largest dataset is ~5,000 frames against 11M images/day; no distributed training, sharded data infra, or throughput/cost engineering.
No TypeScript (soft — they explicitly say they don't care what you're proficient in today).
0 full-time years against a 2–6 year band; all evidence is internships, research fellowships, and coursework capstones.
No cloud infrastructure ownership — SLURM batch compute is not the same as running your own servers.
overstated_by_keywords: 'Deployment' — ONNX/TFLite export and a TensorRT engine are deployment engineering, not a served, monitored production system.
'Cloud' — SLURM/MPI is HPC batch scheduling, not cloud infrastructure or self-hosted serving.
'Embeddings' — matched on transformer attention, not on the embedding/re-ID work the JD actually means.
understated_by_keywords: Classical CV depth never string-matched: wavelet denoising, custom stitching, PSNR-driven tuning is precisely the 'not reaching for a transformer when a filter will do' requirement.
Synthetic data generation with zero manual annotation is a strong answer to 'you decide which problems are worth solving, then take them from raw sensor data' — no keyword captured it.
Multi-sensor roadside-style fusion (camera + dual ToF over I2C mux, range gating) maps directly onto 'multiple other sensors on the road'.
screening_gaps: No production ML ownership — never deployed, monitored, or iterated a model against live traffic, which is the role's stated mission, not a nice-to-have.
Zero full-time years against a 2 to 6 year band, with all evidence from internships and academic capstones.
No experience anywhere near their data volume — about 5,000 frames at most versus 11 million images a day.
llm_analysis.reasoning: The technical overlap on the edge-CV half of this role is unusually specific — Jetson plus TensorRT plus YOLO on real sensor hardware is his capstone, and the classical-CV judgment they ask for is genuinely evidenced at BARC rather than claimed. What is missing is the other half of the mission statement: nothing in the profile has ever shipped, been monitored, or been iterated in production, and that is the exact thing they lead with. Worth an application as a stretch at the bottom of the band, but the production-ownership gap is what a human reader will catch first.
